items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: playing second trumpet in the brass band with Manuel Perez, an onward brass band.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear the original King Oliver Creole jazz band in about 22, 23, with Johnny Dodds and Dewdry at the Lincoln Gardens?

I took Johnny Dodds' place in 24. I knew King Oliver when I was a kid, around New Orleans, playing second trumpet in the brass band with Manuel Perez, an onward brass band. Then I played with King Oliver a couple of times before I went into the Navy, when I was around 16 and 17 years of age. Joe was in his prime then. He'd play these bonkés and things like that and balls. Sure, I knew all the old times, but in 1922, I was in New Orleans. I didn't hear them at the Lincoln Gardens. When we came up there, it was in…

There are a lot of different theories as to why King Oliver asked Louis to join him. A lot of people say that he was scared of Louis, and that he thought that if he had Louis in his own band, he wouldn't be cut. Do you think this is true?

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: They thought it was Manuel Perez.

ctx.x: What about Rudy Jackson? Was he around?

That's right. I played with him in the band also. You see, I came before Bonnie and Paul. Joe said for me in 23. I had a band at Tom Anderson on Ramport and Canal. On Ramport and I was there. And Jimmy Noon came down from Mardi Gras. And we had a hell of a band then. And Bonnie, we were just running sax, you know. And Bonnie was playing ten. I was playing alto and clarinet. And Lewis Russell, Paul Bobbin, Willie San Diego. And I know him at Twyre on trumpet. He was a very nice trumpet player. They thought it was…
